resolutions.rationale:
It is true that no route Derek owns has pi's two-marked-system shape. It is not true that the carve-out lacks live proof.

The script's existing assertions can only pass on pi's OAuth shape if the carve-out ran, so Joel's `anthropic-oauth` run (L6) is that proof. The arithmetic:
- Without the carve-out the budget is 4 − (system[0] + system[1] + tools) = 1.
- At R1, before + 1 = 2 > 1, so pi's marker is removed. "R1 marks recall's block" fails, and so does R1's input bound.
- At H, carry + before = 2 > 1, which is a no-fit, so no carry is placed and "H marks the last block of turn 2's user message" fails.
- With the carve-out the budget is 2 and every one of those passes.

The carve-out's billing was also measured on pi's own OAuth (N6). Nothing needs adding.

settled_findings: `read_H ≥ read_R1(turn 2) + ⌈chars(turn 2's own text)/8⌉` is safe and discriminating for the script's own turns. It holds on N3/N5/N7/N9 with the text each run sent, and live on the change (11,885 and 11,775). It fails on the base (6,852 = 6,852; 0 when turn 2 is long). The table tokenises at about 2 characters a token, so ⌈chars/8⌉ is a lower bound.

Turn 2's first request in the live script is always a recalling request after a quiet turn, because the turn-1 precondition guarantees it. So pi's marker stays on recall's block there, on every covered route.
The carry is one hop by construction. After a handoff the prefix carries no block and pi's own marker serves (N3 turn 3: 9,274 read, 81 written with no carry).
D3's live proof is Joel's `anthropic-oauth` run. Without the carve-out, the R1 and H marker assertions cannot pass on pi's four-point OAuth shape. The billing was measured in N6.

Turn 2's twelve-call compliance is the model's (5 of 9 runs). Rewording, including dropping the output question, did not change it. The precondition stays, and a failing run is re-run under §8.2's rule.
The context handler receives the payload state as a `payloadCache` field of its existing deps object (precedent 402bc0c). There is no new signature exception.

Derek's change to the "shrunk block on the same carried message" expectation, from read rate to write rate, is D8's specified fix: the spec row "cached, and changed in place … the write rate, not the read rate". It is not an expectation edited to make a test pass.
